lessons.title: There’s still time to reach your 2026 money goals
lessons.readingNote: 本页是原创英文学习导读，不是 NPR 节目逐字稿；表达、例句和题目为学习练习，不保证在原节目中逐字出现。
lessons.transcript:
A money goal is easier to revisit when it becomes a small, repeatable task. Imagine that you are in the final months of a year and want to get a sense of where you're at. Start with a simple record of money coming in and money going out. You might notice that small expenses pile up, or that a bill arrives out of the blue. Neither observation is a judgment about you; it is useful information.

Next, choose one goal to chip away at. It could be building an emergency fund, reducing a balance, or setting money aside for a planned expense. Account for bills that are easy to forget, and ask how much money you have left over after essentials. A modest plan that fits your cash flow may be easier to follow than an ambitious plan you cannot maintain.

This is an original English practice passage inspired by the theme of reviewing financial goals. It is not a transcript, quotation, or summary of the exact words spoken in the NPR episode. Open the original episode page to listen and compare the topic with your own plan.

lessons.title: How journaling can help you through hard moments
lessons.readingNote: 本页是原创英文学习导读，不是 NPR 节目逐字稿；表达、例句和题目为学习练习，不保证在原节目中逐字出现。
lessons.transcript:
A private notebook can give you a place to make sense of a difficult week. You do not have to produce a polished story for an audience. The first step may be to put pen to paper and describe one moment that is still on your mind. If a full paragraph feels hard, start small: write a list, a question, or two imperfect sentences.

Writing can help you work through a feeling without requiring you to solve it immediately. Give yourself permission to change your mind as you write. You can describe what happened, what you felt, and what you still do not understand. A short routine after breakfast or before bed may help you get into the habit of returning to the page.

This is an original English practice passage inspired by the theme of journaling. It is not an NPR transcript or a quotation from the episode. The learning expressions and exercises are original practice material; visit the source page for the original audio.

lessons.title: It's open enrollment season. Here's how to make the best decision for you
lessons.readingNote: 本页是原创英文学习导读，不是 NPR 节目逐字稿；表达、例句和题目为学习练习，不保证在原节目中逐字出现。
lessons.transcript:
Choosing a health insurance plan can involve unfamiliar vocabulary. In this practice scenario, a learner compares two imaginary plans. One has a lower monthly premium, but a higher deductible. The other costs more each month and may have different rules for doctors and clinics. The learner decides to look beyond the headline price and factor in how often they might need care.

Before making a choice, the learner reads the fine print. They write down questions about copayments, coinsurance, the provider network, and the out-of-pocket maximum. The costs can add up in different ways, so they compare several possible situations rather than one number. They also check whether their preferred clinic is in network. These questions help them make an informed decision about an imaginary example, not a real policy.

This is an original English practice passage inspired by the theme of comparing insurance plans. It is not an NPR transcript or current insurance advice. Terms and plan rules vary; consult the original episode page and current plan documents for real decisions.

quizzes.q: 表达“权衡不同选择”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: Take a little time to **weigh your options** before choosing a plan.
quizzes.zh: 选方案前，花一点时间权衡不同选择。

quizzes.q: 表达“不只看；超越表面因素”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: I try to **look beyond** the headline price when comparing subscriptions.
quizzes.zh: 比较订阅服务时，我会考虑标价以外的因素。

quizzes.q: 表达“累加；合计”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: Small charges can **add up** over a year.
quizzes.zh: 一整年下来，小额收费也会累积成不少钱。

quizzes.q: 表达“把……纳入考虑”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: We need to **factor in** travel time when choosing a clinic.
quizzes.zh: 选择诊所时，我们需要把路程时间考虑进去。

quizzes.q: 表达“自掏腰包支付”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: I had to **pay out of pocket** for a service my plan did not cover.
quizzes.zh: 有项服务不在我的保险保障范围内，我得自掏腰包。

quizzes.q: 表达“从长远来看”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: A convenient option may save us time **in the long run**.
quizzes.zh: 方便的选择从长远来看可能会节省时间。

quizzes.q: 表达“仔细阅读细则”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: I **read the fine print** before agreeing to the contract.
quizzes.zh: 同意合同之前，我仔细阅读了细则。

quizzes.q: 表达“留出一笔钱；预留资金”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: I **set money aside** each month for unexpected expenses.
quizzes.zh: 我每个月都会留出一笔钱应付意外开支。

quizzes.q: 表达“更清楚地了解”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: A simple comparison table helps me **get a clearer picture of** the costs.
quizzes.zh: 一张简单的比较表能让我更清楚地了解费用。

quizzes.q: 表达“在了解信息后作出决定”时，哪一个短语最合适？
quizzes.en: Asking specific questions helps me **make an informed decision**.
quizzes.zh: 提出具体问题有助于我在了解信息后作出决定。

financeQs.after: is a preferred provider organization plan that generally offers more flexibility in choosing providers.

financeQs.zh: PPO是优选医疗服务组织类方案，通常在选择医疗服务提供者方面更灵活。

financeQs.after: is a high-deductible health plan; the acronym describes its deductible structure.
financeQs.hint: High-Deductible Health Plan；高免赔额健康保险方案
financeQs.zh: HDHP是高免赔额健康保险方案，这个缩写描述了其免赔额结构。

financeQs.after: stands for health savings account.

financeQs.zh: FSA是弹性支出账户的缩写。

prompts.cn: 用选健身房、手机套餐或订阅服务的经历，说明你为什么不只比较标价。
prompts.tip: 列出两个非价格因素，解释它们怎样影响你的决定。
prompts.follow: Which two options did you compare? What did the headline price leave out? Which factor mattered most?
prompts.ex: When choosing a gym, I look beyond the monthly fee and factor in travel time. A nearby gym is easier to use regularly.
prompts.zh: 选健身房时，我不只看月费，也会考虑路程时间。附近的健身房更容易让我坚持去。

prompts.cn: 设想你面对一份条款复杂的合同或方案。你会问哪两个问题，帮助自己作出决定？
prompts.tip: 写出具体问题，例如是否有额外收费或取消条件，而不只说要了解更多。
prompts.follow: Which clause would you check? Who could explain it? How would the answer change your choice?
prompts.ex: I read the fine print to check the cancellation rules. Knowing the extra charges helps me make an informed decision.
prompts.zh: 我仔细阅读细则，核对取消规则。了解额外费用能帮助我作出知情的决定。

prompts.cn: 谈谈你如何为突发开支做准备。可以使用虚构金额，不需要填写真实财务或健康信息。
prompts.tip: 写出一个实际动作，说明为什么小额但持续的准备可能有用。
prompts.follow: What kind of expense might surprise you? What small amount could you reserve? How would you track it?
prompts.ex: I set money aside for unexpected repairs. Small amounts can add up, so I keep a simple record of what I save.
prompts.zh: 我会留出一笔钱应付意外维修。小额资金也能积少成多，所以我会简单记录储蓄情况。
